questions.question: Most of the sculptures in 'Rani ki Vav' are in devotion to ________.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Chemical formula of Ozone is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**O3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Ozone Layer: 

 
• Ozone (O3) is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen. Ozone is a deadly poison.
 
• Ozone is found in the stratosphere layer of the atmosphere.
 
• However, at higher levels of the atmosphere, ozone performs an essential function. It shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
 
• This radiation is highly damaging to organisms, for example, it is known to cause skin cancer in human beings or can split DNA.
 
• It is a pale blue gas with a distinctively pungent smell.
 
• Ozone is an excellent oxidizing agent as it breaks down into oxygen gas and nascent oxygen. { O3 → O2 + [O] }
 
• It is an allotrope of oxygen that is much less stable than the diatomic allotrope O2, breaking down in the lower atmosphere to O2 or di-oxygen

Its depletion:

 
• The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s.
 
• This decrease has been linked to synthetic chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) which are used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
 
• The government bans those products which contain CFCs.

 
• Ozone is thermodynamically unstable and decomposes to molecular oxygen. Thus, a dynamic equilibrium exists between the production and decomposition of ozone molecules

questions.question: Mr. Shah is willing to spend up to Rs. 50 lakh for a German luxury car. Luckily he ﬁnds a dealer who says the price of the car is Rs. 42 lakh. Mr. Shah convinces the dealer to give him a 5% discount on the said price. Mr. Shah's consumer surplus is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 10.1 Lakh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Consumer surplus:-**

 
 
• It s an economic measure of consumer benefit, which is calculated by analyzing the difference between what consumers are willing and able to pay for a good or service relative to its market price, or what they actually do spend on the good or service.
 
 

Hence according to the question,

 
• Consumer surplus = Consumer Willing – Able to Pay + Discount on Able to Pay
 
• = 50 lakhs - 42 lakhs
 
• = 8 lakhs
 
• Discount on Able to Pay = 5%
 
• = 42 lakhs × (5 ÷ 100)
 
• = 2.1 lakhs
 
• Consumer Surplus = 8 lakhs + 2.1 lakhs
 
• = 10.1 lakhs

questions.question: Customs duty is an instrument of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Policy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal policy:-**

 
 
• It is used to stabilize the level of output and employment through changes in expenditure and taxes.
 
• The government attempts to increase output and income and seeks to stabilize the ups and downs in the economy.
 
• Custom or import duties are levied by the Central Government of India on the goods imported into India by using fiscal policy to stabilize the level of input.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary policy:-**

 
 
• Monetary policy can be defined as those actions of the nation's central bank (R.B.I) which helps in controlling the money supply to achieve macroeconomic goals that promote sustainable economic growth.
 
• In simple terms, monetary policy refers to the use of those monetary instruments which under the control of the central bank to regulate interest rates, money supply, and availability of credit to achieve the ultimate objective of economic policy.
 
 
 
• **Trade policy:-**
 
 
• Trade policy refers to the regulations and agreements which control foreign imports and exports.
 
• Such policies are country-specific and are formulated by their elected officials.
 
• A country's trade policy requires import and export taxes, inspection rules, tariffs, and quotas.
 
• Trade policies can take on varying dimensions and complexity depending on the number of political parties involved.

questions.question: Radon is formed in the alpha decay of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ radium.__**

__**Explanation;**__

 
• Radon-222 is formed naturally during a chain of radioactive decay.
 
• The decay series begins with uranium-238, and among the substances formed is radium-226, which decays directly to radon-222.
 
• Uranium is widely distributed in rocks and soils throughout the earth's crust.

questions.question: The circular depression containing a volcanic vent is called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crater.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An impact crater is an approximately circular depression in the surface of a planet, moon, or another solid body in the Solar System or elsewhere, formed by the hypervelocity impact of a smaller body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Smog:-

 
 
• It is the term derived from two words smoke and fog.
 
• It is a kind of intense air pollution.
 
• The word smog was coined in the 20th century. 
 
• Smog is air pollution that reduces visibility.
 
• This kind of visible air pollution is composed of nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, ozone, smoke, and other particulates.
 
• Man-made smog is derived from coal combustion emissions, vehicular emissions, industrial emissions, forest and agricultural fires, and photochemical reactions of these emissions.
 
• Smog is the result of the reaction of emissions from automobiles, factories, and industries with the sunlight and atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Crust**:-​
 
 
• It is the outermost solid part of the earth, normally about 8-40 km thick.
 
• It is brittle in nature. Nearly 1% of the earth’s volume and 5% of the earth’s mass are made of the crust.
 
• The thickness of the crust under the oceanic and continental areas is different. 
 
• The oceanic crust is thinner (about 5kms) as compared to the continental crust (about 30 km).
 
 
 
• **Delta:-**
 
 
• A Delta is a wetland that forms rivers and empties their water and sediment into another body of water such as an ocean, river, or lake.

questions.question: Sikh Khalsa Army was formed under the rule of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranjit Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ranjit singh**

 
 
• Ranjit Singh’s parents were **Mahan Singh Sukerchakia** and **Raj Kaur**..
 
• He expanded his empire by annexing states around him. The Sikh Empire existed from **1799 till 1849**.
 
• The major towns in Ranjit Singh’s empire were **Lahore, Amritsar, Multan, Peshawar, Jammu, Srinagar, Rawalpindi, **and** Sialkot**.
 
• Ranjit Singh was declared the ‘Maharaja of Punjab’ on 12 April 1801.
 
• Ranjit Singh’s army was known as the Khalsa army.
 
• Ranjit Singh, renowned as Sher-e-Punjab (Lion of Punjab), is remembered for the possession of the Koh-i-Noor diamond.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah**

 
 
• Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Suri dynasty.
 
• The silver coin introduced by Sher Shah Suri was called Rupiya.
 
• Sher Shah Suri issued the Rupiya coin and fixed standard weights and measures all over the empire.
 
• This coin introduced by Sher Shah Suri weighed 178 grains and was the precursor of the modern rupee.
 
• Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa and assumed the title of Farid al-Din Sher Shah as emperor in **1539**.
 
• He again defeated the Humayun in the battle of Kannauj and annexed Kannauj in **1540**.
 
• The grand trunk road that turns from Calcutta to Peshawar was built by Sher Shah Suri.
 
 
 
• **Rana Pratap**
 
 
• He belongs to the Sisodias of the Mewar dynasty.
 
• He was titled "Mewari Rana".
 
• The struggle between the Rajput confederacy led by Pratap Singh, and the Mughal Empire under Akbar, has often been characterized as a struggle between Hindus and the invading Muslims.
 
• He fought many battles including the historic battle of ‘Haldighati’ against Raja Mansingh on June 21, 1576.
 
• The Battle of Dewair was a battle fought in 1582 between Mewar forces led by the Maharana Pratap against the Mughal Empire forces of Akbar led by Shabaz Khan in present-day Rajasthan.
 
 
• This battle was won by Maharana Pratap.
 
 
 
 

 
• Hemu vikramaditya

 
 
• He was a Hindu king and had earlier served as a general and chief minister of Adil Shah Suri (Suri dynasty).
 
• He had won 22 battles for Adil Shah Suri defeating the Afghan rebels and Mughal forces of Humayun and Akbar.
 
• He assumed the title of 'Vikramaditya' after taking the control of Delhi.
 
• He was defeated by the Akbar's army in the second battle of Panipat on 5 November 1556.

questions.question: Which device is used to limit electric current in a circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• A Resistor is a device which opposes the flow of charge in the circuit. Hence it is used to limit electric current flow in the circuit.
 
• Whereas Fuse is used to protect the electric Circuit from sudden surges of charge flowing into the circuit.
 
• So, both are in a way, limiting the flow of electric current in a circuit and hence both are the right answer.

questions.question: If a physical quantity has the units - ampere per meter squared, then what are it's dimensions?
questions.solution:
The ampere per meter squared, symbolized A/m², is the International Unit of electric current density.

A current density of 1 A/m² represents one ampere of electric current flowing through a material with a cross-sectional area of one square meter.

ampere per squared meter (A/m²) has a dimension of IL⁻² where L is length, and I is electric current.

questions.question: Who conducts oath of office to the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The chief Justice of India.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The chief justice of India** makes the oath or affirmation to the President of India.
 
• In the absence of the chief justice,** the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is available for the oath.**
 
• **Article 60 **talks about oath or affirmation by the President.
 
• The tenure of the President is** 5 years.**
 
• He is appointed by **the electoral college.**
 
• He can resign by writing to **the Vice-President.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

Prime Minister: 

 
• In the scheme of the parliamentary system of government provided by the constitution, the President is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive) and Prime Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive).
 
• In other words, the president is the head of the State while Prime Minister is the head of the government. ​

**Lok Sabha Speaker:**

 
• The Lok Sabha speaker is the presiding officer or head of Lok Sabha.
 
• He is the guardian of the powers and privileges of members and committees of Lok Sabha.
 
• President appoints a Protem Speaker for the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.
 
• He is appointed to administer the oath to the new members and enable the house to elect a new speaker. Usually, the senior-most member is elected as a Protem speaker and the President himself administers the oath to him.

 **Chairman of Rajya Sabha:**

 
• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The term of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is only 5 years.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

• Some important book

• **R. K. Narayan:-**

 
 
• He was born in 1906 in Madras and began his writing career with *Swami and Friends (1935).*
 
• He created the fictional town Malgudi which became the setting for most of his short stories.
 
• All the stories in *Malgudi Days* are narrated by an unnamed narrator and his stories reveal features of realism, subtle social criticism, and allegory.
 
• He has won many awards such as Sahitya Akademi Award and Padma Bhushan.

questions.question: Which is the longest canal in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grand Canal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Grand Canal** located between** Beijing-Hangzhou in China**, **is the longest artificial river or canal in the world.**
 
• It has been also listed as a **World Heritage Site by UNESCO** during the Conference on **World Heritage in 2014.**
 
• The Grand Canal’s total length is **approximately 1,104 miles** while its greatest height is** 138 feet **at the summit of Shandong Mountain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Panama Canal was created in 1914 and is 77 km long connecting two oceans, the Atlantic and the Pacific. 
 
• The Corinth Canal connects the Gulf of Corinth in the Ionian Sea with the Saronic Gulf in the Aegean Sea.
 
• **The Welland Canal** is a ship canal in Ontario, Canada, connecting Lake Ontario and Lake Erie.

questions.question: In fertilisation of a flower, the fertilised central cell will develop into ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**endosperm.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• In fertilization of a flower, one sperm nucleus fertilizes the egg cell, forming a zygote, while the other sperm nucleus usually fuses with the binucleate central cell, forming a primary endosperm cell (its nucleus is often called the triple fusion nucleus). That cell created in the process of double fertilization develops into the endosperm.
 
• The most important and unique characteristic of angiosperms is the participation of both male gametes in the act of fertilization. One male gamete fuses with the egg cell and forms the diploid Zygote. The process is called syngamy or generative fertilization. The Zygote (2n) develops into an embryo.
 
• The other male gamete fuses with two polar nuclei (or secondary nuclei) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus. The process is known as triple fusion or Vegetative fertilization. 
 
• These two actions of fertilization are together called Double Fertilization

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1768bf0dcc7ddb051b0c4b63f599bfcd04fe84287f417234ca680f984f9d629a.png]
